rows.question: When does my maternity leave start if my due date is 15 November 2026?
rows.reply:
Under the Mutterschutz (statutory maternity protection period) rules, the period before birth covers "die letzten sechs Wochen vor der Entbindung", the last six weeks before the birth (MuSchG §3(1)). It is calculated from the expected date of delivery shown in the certificate from your doctor, midwife or Entbindungspfleger, not from the actual birth (MuSchG §3(1)).

With an expected date of 15 November 2026, the six weeks are counted back from that date, which puts the start in early October 2026. The excerpts do not say how the first day is counted, so check the exact date with your employer or your health insurance fund, using the date on your certificate.

What the period before birth means:
- Your employer may not employ you during these six weeks unless you expressly declare that you are willing to work. You can withdraw that declaration at any time, with effect for the future (MuSchG §3(1)).
- If the baby is not born on the expected day, the period before birth becomes shorter or longer accordingly (MuSchG §3(1)).
- You should tell your employer about the pregnancy and the expected date of delivery as soon as you know. If your employer asks, you should provide a certificate from a doctor or midwife that states the expected date (MuSchG §15).

After the birth, your employer may not employ you until eight weeks after the birth have passed. This rises to twelve weeks in three cases: "1. bei Frühgeburten, 2. bei Mehrlingsgeburten" and 3. if a disability of the child is medically established within eight weeks of the birth. In the third case, the extension applies only if you apply for it. If the baby is born early, the period after birth is also extended by the time that was lost from the period before birth (MuSchG §3(2)).

Mutterschaftsgeld (maternity pay) from statutory health insurance is paid for the protection periods and for the day of delivery. For payment before the birth, the certificate from a doctor or midwife stating the expected date is decisive (SGB V §24i(3)).

Mutterschutz is separate from Elternzeit (parental leave). Under BEEG §16(1), Elternzeit must be requested from your employer in text form. For the period up to the child's third birthday, the request must be made at least seven weeks before the Elternzeit begins.

rows.question: How long after birth can we apply for Elterngeld without losing money?
rows.reply:
The law does not set an application deadline. It limits how far back payment goes, and that limit is what costs money.

Elterngeld (parental allowance) must be applied for in writing. It is paid retroactively only for the last three Lebensmonate before the start of the Lebensmonat in which the application was received: "rückwirkend nur für die letzten drei Lebensmonate vor Beginn des Lebensmonats geleistet, in dem der Antrag auf Elterngeld eingegangen ist" (BEEG §7(1)). Any earlier Lebensmonate are not paid. What counts is when the application is received, not when it is sent.

This matters because Elterngeld can be drawn from the day of birth (BEEG §4(1)), and it is paid in monthly amounts (Monatsbeträge) for the child's Lebensmonate (BEEG §4(2)). An application that arrives late loses whole months of payment from the start of that period.

The periods in which it can be drawn are set by BEEG §4(1). Basiselterngeld can be drawn until the child completes the 14th Lebensmonat. Elterngeld Plus can be drawn until the child completes the 32nd Lebensmonat, as long as at least one parent draws it in consecutive Lebensmonate from the 15th Lebensmonat onward.

The same three-month limit applies to changing an application later. A change can be claimed retroactively only for the last three Lebensmonate before the start of the Lebensmonat in which the change request was received (BEEG §7(2)).

The excerpts do not define how a Lebensmonat is counted. Your Elterngeldstelle decides on Elterngeld applications, and it is where a binding answer on your own case comes from (familienportal.de).

rows.question: How much notice do I have to give my employer for Elternzeit?
rows.reply:
Elternzeit (parental leave (unpaid job-protected leave)) is requested from your employer, and the notice period depends on when the leave falls (BEEG §16(1)).

- For leave up to the child's third birthday: at least seven weeks before the leave begins ("spätestens sieben Wochen").
- For leave between the third birthday and the child's eighth birthday: at least 13 weeks before the leave begins ("spätestens 13 Wochen").

The request must be made in text form ("in Textform vom Arbeitgeber verlangen"). The Familienportal says this can be, for example, a letter without a signature or an email.

Other rules in the same section:

- If you request leave up to the third birthday, you must say at the same time for which periods within two years you will take Elternzeit.
- Where there are urgent reasons, a reasonably shorter notice period is possible as an exception ("Bei dringenden Gründen ist ausnahmsweise eine angemessene kürzere Frist möglich").
- If the mother takes Elternzeit straight after the maternity protection period under §3(2) and (3) of the Mutterschutzgesetz, that period counts towards the two-year period. If she takes it after annual leave that follows the maternity protection period, both the protection period and the annual leave count towards it.
- If a mother cannot request leave in time for leave starting straight after the maternity protection period, for a reason she is not responsible for, she can make the request within one week after that reason ends (BEEG §16(2)).
- The employer must certify the Elternzeit to you ("Der Arbeitgeber hat ... die Elternzeit zu bescheinigen").

The timing also affects protection from dismissal. From the point at which Elternzeit has been requested, the employer may not give notice of dismissal. This protection starts at the earliest eight weeks before leave up to the third birthday. For leave between the third and eighth birthdays, it starts at the earliest 14 weeks before (BEEG §18(1)).

The Familienportal page also states that for births before 1 July 2015, a seven-week period applies whether the leave is before or after the third birthday. The statutory transitional provision for earlier births is not among these excerpts. That page is guidance, not the statute.

rows.question: How long is maternity protection after the birth if the baby comes early?
rows.reply:
Under federal law, the Mutterschutz (statutory maternity protection period) after the birth is normally eight weeks. The employer may not employ the mother until eight weeks after the birth ("bis zum Ablauf von acht Wochen nach der Entbindung", MuSchG §3(2)).

An early birth can lengthen this in two separate ways.

1. The 8 weeks are extended by the days lost before the birth. The protection period before the birth is the last six weeks before the expected date of delivery. If the baby comes before that date, the pre-birth period is shortened (MuSchG §3(1)). The statute then extends the post-birth period by the length of that shortening: "Bei vorzeitiger Entbindung verlängert sich die Schutzfrist nach der Entbindung … um den Zeitraum der Verkürzung der Schutzfrist vor der Entbindung" (MuSchG §3(2)). The official Familienportal page explains that the total period therefore stays at 14 weeks. It ends as many days after the 8 weeks as the baby arrived before the expected date.

2. The 8 weeks become 12 weeks in three cases. The statute lists all three (MuSchG §3(2)):
- "bei Frühgeburten" (premature births);
- "bei Mehrlingsgeburten" (multiple births);
- where a disability within the meaning of SGB IX §2(1) is medically established in the child before the end of eight weeks after the birth. This third extension applies only if the woman applies for it. The Familienportal page says the application is made to the health insurance fund (Krankenkasse).

The statute says the 12-week extension does not apply to a stillbirth.

The extension for the shortened pre-birth period applies on top of the 12 weeks as well. The statute applies it to the 8-week period and to the 12-week period alike ("nach Satz 1 oder nach Satz 2"). The Familienportal page states that for a premature birth the total period rises from 14 to 18 weeks.

The statute uses the word Frühgeburt without defining it in the excerpts available here. The Familienportal page describes it as a baby born so early that it medically counts as premature, giving as an example a birth weight under 2,500 grams. Not every birth before the expected date is a Frühgeburt in this sense. An early birth that is not medically premature gets the first extension only.

After the birth, the period cannot be waived. The Familienportal page calls it an absolute employment ban. The only exception is for pupils and students, who may resume their training activity if they expressly ask (MuSchG §3(3)). If an employer demands work during the period, the Familienportal page says you can turn to your supervisory authority (Aufsichtsbehörde).

rows.question: Can my employer dismiss me while I am pregnant?
rows.reply:
Only in exceptional cases, and only with an authority's prior approval. The rule is in MuSchG §17.

When dismissal is not allowed. Under MuSchG §17(1), dismissing a woman is not permitted ("Die Kündigung gegenüber einer Frau ist unzulässig"):
1. during her pregnancy,
2. until four months after a miscarriage after the twelfth week of pregnancy, and
3. until the end of her protection period after the birth, and in any case until four months after the birth.

This Kündigungsschutz (protection against dismissal) applies if the employer knows about the pregnancy, miscarriage or birth when dismissing you, or if you tell the employer within two weeks after you receive the dismissal. Missing those two weeks does no harm if the delay is for a reason you are not responsible for and you give the information without delay. The same rules apply to steps the employer takes to prepare a dismissal. The Familienportal adds that the protection also applies if you did not yet know you were pregnant, but you must already have been pregnant when you received the dismissal.

The exception. Under MuSchG §17(2), the highest state authority responsible for occupational safety, or a body it designates, can exceptionally declare a dismissal admissible. This applies only in special cases that are not connected with your condition during pregnancy, after a miscarriage after the twelfth week, or after the birth. Such a dismissal must be in writing and must state the reason. The Familienportal gives these examples of special reasons:
- the company is insolvent;
- the business is partly closed;
- in a small business, it cannot continue without a qualified replacement;
- you have committed a particularly serious breach of duty.

The employer must apply in writing to the supervisory authority. Without its approval, the dismissal is invalid.

If you are dismissed without approval. According to the Familienportal, you must file a claim with the competent labour court to have the dismissal declared invalid. The claim must normally be filed within 3 weeks of receiving the written dismissal ("normalerweise innerhalb von 3 Wochen … ab Erhalt der schriftlichen Kündigung"). If you do not file a claim, the dismissal counts as effective. You can file the claim yourself or through a representative such as a lawyer. You can also make it orally, for the record, at the court's office ("mündlich zu Protokoll der Geschäftsstelle"). The Familienportal says you should also involve the competent supervisory authority.

If you are dismissed with approval. You can challenge the approval itself. Depending on the Bundesland, this is done by an objection or by a lawsuit. This is a separate procedure. It does not replace the claim at the labour court and cannot on its own keep your employment in place.

Related points from the excerpts:
- If you take parental leave after the birth, the protection can be extended (BEEG §18).
- On a fixed-term contract, maternity protection lasts as long as the contract runs and ends when the contract ends.
- You may yourself resign during pregnancy, with your contractual notice period.

Whether a particular dismissal is valid is not decided here. It is decided by the labour court, and approval of an exceptional dismissal is decided by the supervisory authority in your state. The Familienportal says you can also contact that authority with questions about maternity protection.

rows.question: Is there an income limit above which we get no Elterngeld?
rows.reply:
Yes. For Elterngeld (parental allowance), the statute sets an income limit above which the entitlement is lost.

The rule in BEEG §1(8): the entitlement lapses ("Ein Anspruch entfällt") if the entitled person had a zu versteuerndes Einkommen (taxable income) under §2(5) of the Income Tax Act of "mehr als 175 000 Euro" in the last completed tax assessment period before the child's birth. If another person also lives in a household with the child, or qualifies under §1(3) or (4), the limit applies to the combined taxable income of both: the entitlement lapses if the sum is more than 175,000 euros.

The limit uses taxable income, not gross income. The federal guidance page says gross income is usually considerably higher. Taxable income is what remains after special expenses, provident expenses, individual allowances and extraordinary burdens are deducted from total income. The Finanzamt determines it and states it in the tax assessment notice.

Earlier births may fall under different limits. The same guidance page says the limit was 200,000 euros for births from 1 April 2024. It says it was 300,000 euros for couples and 250,000 euros for single parents for births from 1 September 2021 to 31 March 2024. Those figures come from a guidance page, not from the statute. The statute's transitional provision for earlier births is not among the excerpts I have, so I cannot say which limit governs a particular birth.

If it is not yet clear whether the limit is exceeded, you can still apply.
- The guidance page says the tax assessment notice for the calendar year before the birth should be attached to the application, if available.
- Under BEEG §8(2), if that notice is not available and the application indicates the limits will probably not be exceeded, Elterngeld is paid subject to revocation if they turn out to be exceeded.
- Under BEEG §8(3) no. 1, if it cannot yet be said whether the limits are exceeded, the amount is decided provisionally.

Whether the limit applies to your family, and which limit governs your child's birth, is decided by the Elterngeldstelle. The Elterngeldstelle for your district is where you get a binding answer on your own case.

rows.question: How many months of Elterngeld can we get in total?
rows.reply:
BEEG §4 sets the number of months that applies to every family.

Basiselterngeld. Elterngeld (parental allowance) comes as Basiselterngeld or Elterngeld Plus (BEEG §4(1)). Together, parents are entitled to "zwölf Monatsbeträge Basiselterngeld", 12 monthly payments (BEEG §4(3)). If one parent's earned income is reduced in two Lebensmonate, the parents together get two more months, called Partnermonate, making 14 (BEEG §4(3)).

Elterngeld Plus. Instead of one Lebensmonat of Basiselterngeld, a parent can take two Lebensmonate of Elterngeld Plus (BEEG §4(3)).

Limits per parent. One parent can have at most 12 monthly payments of Basiselterngeld, plus at most four monthly payments of Partnerschaftsbonus under §4b (BEEG §4(4)). §4b itself is not among these excerpts. The official guidance says each parent can get up to 4 extra months of ElterngeldPlus as Partnerschaftsbonus if both work part-time at the same time (familienportal.de). A parent only has a claim if they take Elterngeld for at least two Lebensmonate (BEEG §4(4)).

When the months can be taken. Basiselterngeld can be taken until the child completes the 14th Lebensmonat. Elterngeld Plus can be taken until the 32nd Lebensmonat, as long as at least one parent takes it in consecutive Lebensmonate from the 15th (BEEG §4(1)). The guidance adds that if, after the 14th Lebensmonat, there is a month in which neither parent receives ElterngeldPlus, none can be received afterwards, even with months left over (familienportal.de).

How months are counted. Elterngeld is paid "in Monatsbeträgen für Lebensmonate des Kindes" (BEEG §4(2)). The guidance says these are not calendar months. They start from the day of birth: for a child born on 15 February, the 1st Lebensmonat runs from 15 February to 14 March (familienportal.de).

Months used up without being claimed. Both parents can draw Basiselterngeld at the same time in only one of the first twelve Lebensmonate (BEEG §4(6)). The guidance says such a month counts as 2 Basiselterngeld months used (familienportal.de). Lebensmonate in which a parent is due certain benefits that are offset against Elterngeld count as Basiselterngeld months for that parent (BEEG §4(4)). The guidance says this covers the mother's Mutterschaftsgeld months, whether or not Basiselterngeld is applied for (familienportal.de).

Premature births. For a child born early, the joint claim to Basiselterngeld is higher (BEEG §4(5)). The early-birth period is measured from the expected delivery date shown in the medical or midwife's certificate.
- At least 6 weeks early: 13 monthly payments.
- At least 8 weeks early: 14.
- At least 12 weeks early: 15.
- At least 16 weeks early: 16.

In these cases the per-parent maximum rises to 13, 14, 15 or 16 monthly payments respectively, each plus up to four of Partnerschaftsbonus. The period for Basiselterngeld extends to the 15th, 16th, 17th or 18th Lebensmonat. Elterngeld Plus still runs to the 32nd Lebensmonat, taken in consecutive months from the 16th, 17th, 18th or 19th (BEEG §4(5)).

In the application. The application must state which Lebensmonate are claimed as Basiselterngeld, Elterngeld Plus or Partnerschaftsbonus (BEEG §7(1)). If the other parent has neither applied nor notified the authority of their months, all monthly payments go to the parent who applied. The other parent can later receive only what remains of the joint total (BEEG §7(3)).

How many of these months your family receives, and how they are split, is decided only by the Elterngeldstelle responsible for you. That office is where you get a binding answer on your own case.

rows.question: What is the Partnerschaftsbonus and who qualifies?
rows.reply:
The Partnerschaftsbonus (partnership bonus months) gives each parent additional monthly amounts of Elterngeld Plus. This applies when both parents work part-time at the same time. The source is BEEG §4b.

The conditions in the statute (BEEG §4b(1)):
1. Both parents are in paid work for "nicht weniger als 24 und nicht mehr als 32 Wochenstunden im Durchschnitt des Lebensmonats". That means at least 24 and at most 32 hours a week, averaged over the Lebensmonat.
2. Both parents meet the general Elterngeld requirements of BEEG §1.

When both conditions hold, each parent is entitled to one additional monthly amount of Elterngeld Plus for that Lebensmonat.

Further rules in BEEG §4b:
- Each parent can receive at most four monthly amounts of Partnerschaftsbonus. It can only be received if taken for at least two Lebensmonate (§4b(2)).
- The parents can receive it only at the same time and in consecutive Lebensmonate (§4b(3)).
- The consecutive-months requirement still counts as met if it later turns out that the conditions were not present in every month for which the Partnerschaftsbonus was applied for (§4b(5)).
- If, during receipt, one of the situations in BEEG §4c(1) Nr. 1 to 3 arises, one parent can continue receiving it alone under §4c(2) (§4b(4)).

One parent alone (BEEG §4c(2)). A single parent is entitled to additional monthly amounts of Elterngeld Plus where one of these three situations applies:
1. That parent meets the conditions for the tax relief for single parents under §24b(1) and (3) of the Einkommensteuergesetz, and the other parent lives neither with them nor with the child.
2. Care by the other parent would endanger the child's welfare within the meaning of §1666(1) and (2) BGB.
3. Care by the other parent is impossible, in particular because of serious illness or severe disability. Economic reasons and being prevented by other activities do not count.

The parent must also work 24 to 32 hours a week on average in at least two and at most four consecutive Lebensmonate.

What the federal Familienportal adds (guidance, not statute):
- Separated parents can also receive the Partnerschaftsbonus.
- It can be used before, between or after the other Elterngeld months, and also if you otherwise receive only Basiselterngeld.
- It is calculated the same way as Elterngeld Plus. The page states between 150 and 900 euros per parent per month, depending on income before the birth. The excerpt does not give the date this figure was checked.
- If your average hours in a Lebensmonat differ from what you planned, you must report this to your Elterngeldstelle.
- If either parent works fewer than 24 or more than 32 hours in a month, both lose the bonus for that month and it must be repaid. Other months are not affected if the conditions were met in at least two months.

rows.question: We forgot to apply for Kindergeld. How far back will they pay?
rows.reply:
Kindergeld (child benefit) is paid out retroactively for at most the last six months before the start of the month in which the Familienkasse receives the application. The statute says: "Die Auszahlung von festgesetztem Kindergeld erfolgt rückwirkend nur für die letzten sechs Monate vor Beginn des Monats, in dem der Antrag auf Kindergeld eingegangen ist" (EStG §70(1) sentence 2). Months further back than that are not paid out. The same provision adds that the entitlement itself is not affected by this limit on payment: "Der Anspruch auf Kindergeld nach § 62 bleibt von dieser Auszahlungsbeschränkung unberührt" (EStG §70(1) sentence 3). Because the count runs from the month the application arrives, each month of delay moves the six-month window forward.

Kindergeld must be applied for in writing (BKGG §9(1)). The Familienportal says it can be applied for electronically or in writing, and that for a retroactive claim you state in the application that you are applying retroactively and from when you want Kindergeld. The application should be made to the competent Familienkasse (BKGG §9(1)). The Familienportal names this as the Familienkasse of your Agentur für Arbeit, and gives the free Bundesagentur für Arbeit service line for application questions: 0800 4 555530.

Whether your family is entitled, and for which months payment is actually made, is decided by the Familienkasse. It is where a binding answer on your own case comes from.

rows.question: How much Kindergeld do we get per month for our first child?
rows.reply:
The law sets one monthly amount for every child, so the first child gets the same as any other. EStG §66(1) states: "Das Kindergeld beträgt monatlich für jedes Kind 259 Euro." That is 259 euros of Kindergeld (child benefit) per month for each child. BKGG §6(1) states the same figure in the same words. The excerpts do not show the date this figure was last checked, so confirm it against the source before relying on it.

Kindergeld is paid monthly from the beginning of the month in which the conditions are met until the end of the month in which they cease to be met (EStG §66(2)).

The law also provides for increases. If the tax allowances for children are raised, Kindergeld is raised accordingly and rounded to full euros (EStG §66(3)).

At the annual income tax assessment, the Finanzamt checks whether the tax allowances for children or the Kindergeld paid is more favourable for the parents. This check happens automatically and does not need to be requested.

Whether you are entitled is not decided here. The Familienkasse checks the conditions and is where you get a binding answer on your own case. The Familienportal says the application can be made online with the Bundesagentur für Arbeit.

rows.question: How quickly do we have to register the birth at the Standesamt?
rows.reply:
The law requires the birth to be reported within one week. PStG §18(1) says the birth of a child must be reported to the Standesamt (civil registry office) for the area where the child was born "binnen einer Woche" (within one week).

Who reports, and how, under the same provision:
- the persons named in PStG §19 report orally or in writing, and must make the birth credible ("glaubhaft zu machen");
- the institutions named in PStG §20 report in writing.

If a child is stillborn, the report must be made at the latest on the third working day after the birth ("spätestens am dritten auf die Geburt folgenden Werktag").

Where the birth happens matters for what you do yourself, according to the Familienportal:
- after a birth in a hospital, birth centre or maternity clinic, the institution notifies the responsible Standesamt and sends it the birth certificate from the birth;
- after a home birth, the midwife or doctor issues that certificate, and you must present it to the responsible Standesamt within one week.

A Familienportal checklist phrases the period as "innerhalb von 7 Werktagen" (within 7 working days). The statute says "binnen einer Woche", and the statute is what governs.

The excerpts do not say what happens if the report is late. The Standesamt for the place of birth is where the birth is registered and where you can ask about your own case.

rows.question: Which Standesamt do we go to — the one where we live or where the hospital is?
rows.reply:
It is the Standesamt (civil registry office) for the place where your child is born, not the one where you live. The federal family portal says you must register your child within 1 week at the Standesamt "das für den Geburtsort des Kindes zuständig ist" (responsible for the child's place of birth). The portal's birth checklist puts the same step as "innerhalb von 7 Werktagen" (within 7 working days). Neither page describes this period as a statutory deadline or states what happens if it is missed.

If your child is born in a hospital, birth centre or maternity clinic, the facility notifies the responsible Standesamt and sends it the certificate of birth. You tell the facility the first name and surname you want, and it passes them on to the Standesamt.

If your child is born at home, the midwife or doctor issues the certificate of birth, and you must present it to the responsible Standesamt within 1 week. You also give the name directly to that Standesamt.

Your place of residence comes in afterwards. The Standesamt passes the registration on to the residents' registration office automatically.

The portal says the other documents you need are listed on the website of the Standesamt in the town where your child is born. That Standesamt is also where you get a binding answer on your own registration.

rows.question: What do we need to bring to the Standesamt to register the birth?
rows.reply:
The federal rule is in PStV §33. When a birth is reported, the Standesamt (civil registry office) "soll verlangen" (should require) these documents:

1. If the parents are married to each other: their marriage certificate or a certified extract from the marriage register. Also their own birth certificates, if the parents' birth registration details do not appear on the marriage certificate. The marriage certificate must be shown even if the marriage has ended.
2. If the parents are not married to each other: the mother's birth certificate. If paternity has already been acknowledged, also the declarations of acknowledgement and the father's birth certificate, and any declarations of joint parental custody ("Sorgeerklärungen").
3. An identity card, passport or other recognised passport substitute for the parents.
4. If the birth is reported orally: a certificate of birth issued by a doctor, midwife or male midwife who was present at the birth.

PStV §33 also says the Standesamt may ask for further documents where they are needed to prove the details given.

The Familienportal adds some practical points:

- You need the birth certificate issued at the birth ("Geburtsbescheinigung").
- If the child was born in a hospital, birth centre or maternity clinic, that institution notifies the responsible Standesamt and sends it the Geburtsbescheinigung.
- After a home birth, the midwife or doctor issues the Geburtsbescheinigung, and you must present it to the responsible Standesamt within 1 week.

The portal says the child must be registered within 1 week at the Standesamt for the place of birth. Its checklist page says "innerhalb von 7 Werktagen" (within 7 working days). Any further documents required are listed on the website of the Standesamt in the place where the child is born.

If the parents are foreign nationals, PStV §34 also applies. When the birth is reported, the Standesamt asks for information on whether a parent holds an unlimited right of residence ("unbefristetes Aufenthaltsrecht"). It also asks whether a parent holds a residence permit under the 1999 EU–Switzerland free movement agreement, as a Swiss national or a family member of one. The Standesamt uses this to check whether the child acquired German citizenship by birth under StAG §4(3). It obtains written information from the Ausländerbehörde to verify this, and it makes that check itself. If the parents give no such information, or the Standesamt doubts it, it requests the information for both parents.

The Standesamt for the place of birth decides which documents it needs in your case. It is where you get a binding answer on that.

rows.question: Does my Krankenkasse pay for a midwife?
rows.reply:
Yes, if you are insured with a Krankenkasse (statutory health insurer), the law gives you a right to midwife care. Under SGB V §24d, an insured woman is entitled, during pregnancy, at the birth and after the birth, to medical care and to care from a Hebamme (midwife). This includes the examinations to confirm the pregnancy and the check-ups during pregnancy.

Midwife care after the birth has a time limit. The entitlement lasts "bis zum Ablauf von zwölf Wochen nach der Geburt" (until twelve weeks after the birth). Care beyond that requires a doctor's order ("bedürfen der ärztlichen Anordnung").

If the mother cannot care for the child after the birth, the insured child is itself entitled to the midwife services that relate to the child (SGB V §24d).

The Familienportal says the same: every woman with statutory health insurance is entitled to support from a midwife. If you have private health insurance instead, it advises you to check with your insurer beforehand which services it covers. These sources do not say what a private policy pays.

Whether a particular service is covered in your case is decided by your Krankenkasse. Your Krankenkasse is where you get a binding answer on your own case.

rows.question: How do we insure the baby after the birth?
rows.reply:
The excerpts describe how a child is insured under statutory health insurance through Familienversicherung (family cover for dependants under statutory insurance). Under SGB V §10(1), the children of members of a statutory health insurer are insured if the child:
1. has their residence or habitual abode in Germany,
2. is not insured under certain provisions of § 5(1) and is not voluntarily insured,
3. is not exempt from insurance and has not been released from compulsory insurance,
4. is not self-employed as a main occupation, and
5. has no total income that regularly exceeds one seventh of the monthly reference value under § 18 SGB IV.

Under §10(2) no. 1, children are insured up to their 18th birthday. Longer periods apply in the cases listed in §10(2) nos. 2 to 4.

There is one exception that matters around birth. Under §10(3), children are not insured if the parent's spouse or civil partner who is related to the child is not a member of a Krankenkasse, and that parent's total income regularly exceeds one twelfth of the "Jahresarbeitsentgeltgrenze" each month and is regularly higher than the member's income.

If both parents meet the conditions, the member chooses the Krankenkasse (§10(5)).

How it is done: under §10(6), the member must report the insured family members, with the details needed to carry out the Familienversicherung, to the competent Krankenkasse. Later changes to those details must be reported too. A uniform procedure and uniform reporting forms are set by the Spitzenverband Bund der Krankenkassen.

You will need the birth certificate to register the child with the Krankenkasse. After the birth, the child must be registered within 1 week at the Standesamt responsible for the place of birth, which issues the birth certificate.

Whether your child meets these conditions is not something this service can assess. Your competent Krankenkasse is where the report is made and where you get an answer on your own child's cover. rows.question: When are the first check-ups for the baby?
rows.reply:
The Kinder-Richtlinie (the Federal Joint Committee's guideline on early detection of illness in children) provides ten early-detection check-ups in the first six years of life. Each one can only be used within its set period, allowing for a tolerance window: 'können nur in den jeweils angegebenen Zeiträumen unter Berücksichtigung folgender Toleranzgrenzen in Anspruch genommen werden'.

The first check-ups:
- U1: immediately after birth ('Unmittelbar nach der Geburt'). It should be done within the first 30 minutes after the birth. If no doctor is present but a midwife is, the midwife should do it. The U1 has no tolerance window.
- U2: 3rd to 10th day of life ('3.-10. Lebenstag'). Tolerance window: 3rd to 14th day.
- U3: 4th to 5th week of life ('4.-5. Lebenswoche'). Tolerance window: 3rd to 8th week.
- U4: 3rd to 4th month of life ('3.-4. Lebensmonat'). Tolerance window: 2nd to 4½ month.
- U5: 6th to 7th month of life. Tolerance window: 5th to 8th month.
- U6: 10th to 12th month of life. Tolerance window: 9th to 14th month.

The later check-ups are:
- U7: 21st to 24th month. Tolerance window: 20th to 27th.
- U7a: 34th to 36th month. Tolerance window: 33rd to 38th.
- U8: 46th to 48th month. Tolerance window: 43rd to 50th.
- U9: 60th to 64th month. Tolerance window: 58th to 66th.

The same periods apply to babies born prematurely. The prematurity is taken into account when the results are assessed ('Auch bei Frühgeborenen sind die Untersuchungszeiträume einzuhalten').

These periods come from the version of the guideline in force from 1 January 2026. The Federal Joint Committee's page says the version it offers does not yet include a decision that came into force on 20 August 2026. Check the current version on the Federal Joint Committee's website.

rows.question: What is Mutterschaftsgeld and when do I apply for it?
rows.reply:
Mutterschaftsgeld (maternity pay from the health insurer) is a payment for the maternity protection periods ("Schutzfristen") before and after the birth, and for the day of birth itself (MuSchG §19, SGB V §24i(3)).

Who receives it:
- A woman who is a member of a statutory health insurer receives it under the rules of the Fifth Book of the Social Code (SGB V) or the Second Act on Farmers' Health Insurance (MuSchG §19(1)).
- Under SGB V §24i(1), it goes to members who are entitled to Krankengeld when unable to work, or who are not paid wages because of the protection periods under §3 of the Maternity Protection Act. It also goes to women whose employment ends immediately before the protection period begins, if they were members of a health insurer on the last day of employment.
- A woman who is not a member of a statutory health insurer receives it at federal expense, up to 210 euros in total. It is paid "auf Antrag" (on application) by the Bundesamt für Soziale Sicherung (MuSchG §19(2)).

How the amount is set (the rule, not your amount):
- For members who are employed when the pre-birth protection period begins, it is the average daily net pay of the last three settled calendar months before that period. It is "höchstens 13 Euro für den Kalendertag" (at most 13 euros per calendar day) (SGB V §24i(2)).
- Any pay above 13 euros a day is covered by the employer, or by the body responsible for paying Mutterschaftsgeld, under the Maternity Protection Act (SGB V §24i(2)). This is the employer's top-up, the Zuschuss zum Mutterschaftsgeld (MuSchG §20(1)).
- For other members, it is paid at the level of Krankengeld (SGB V §24i(2)).
- The entitlement is suspended while the member receives contributory pay, earned income or holiday compensation. One-off payments are excepted (SGB V §24i(4)).

When it is paid: the official family portal says the protection periods "beginnen normalerweise 6 Wochen vor dem errechneten Geburtstermin und enden 8 Wochen nach der Geburt". That means they normally begin 6 weeks before the expected due date and end 8 weeks after the birth (familienportal.de). For payment before the birth, the decisive document is a certificate from a doctor or a midwife stating the expected day of birth (SGB V §24i(3)).

When to apply: the excerpts I have do not state when to apply to a health insurer, so I cannot give a date. If you have statutory health insurance, your Krankenkasse (health insurer) is where to ask. If you are not a member of a statutory health insurer, the application goes to the Bundesamt für Soziale Sicherung (MuSchG §19(2)).

Related: Mutterschaftsgeld under SGB V and the employer's top-up under MuSchG §20 are counted against Elterngeld. The 210-euro payment under MuSchG §19(2) is not counted (BEEG §3(1)).

rows.question: We are not married. Is my partner automatically the legal father?
rows.reply:
No. Being unmarried means your partner is not automatically the legal father. BGB §1592 says the father of a child is the man who: 1. is married to the child's mother at the time of the birth ("zum Zeitpunkt der Geburt mit der Mutter des Kindes verheiratet ist"); 2. has acknowledged paternity ("die Vaterschaft anerkannt hat"); or 3. has had his paternity established by a court under §1600d BGB or §182(1) of the Act on Proceedings in Family Matters (FamFG).

The Familienportal says the same in plain terms: if he is not married to the mother at the time of the birth, he must make a Vaterschaftsanerkennung (acknowledgement of paternity) to count legally as the father. It is voluntary and needs the mother's consent ("bedarf der Zustimmung der Mutter").

Rules on when it takes effect (BGB §1594):
- It can be made before the child is born ("schon vor der Geburt des Kindes zulässig").
- It is not effective while another man's paternity exists.

rows.question: How do unmarried parents get joint custody?
rows.reply:
Under federal law, if the parents are not married to each other when the child is born, the mother has parental custody (BGB §1626a(3): "Im Übrigen hat die Mutter die elterliche Sorge"). Unmarried parents can have joint custody in three ways.

BGB §1626a(1) says parents who are not married at the birth have joint custody:
1. if they declare that they want to take on custody jointly (Sorgeerklärungen),
2. if they marry each other, or
3. to the extent that the family court transfers custody to them jointly.

First, the father must be legally recognised. The official guidance explains that he becomes the legally recognised father either by acknowledging the child as his own with the mother's consent, or when a court establishes paternity. Acknowledging paternity does not by itself give him custody. A Sorgeerklärung or a court decision is also needed.

Route 1: Sorgeerklärung (declaration of joint custody). Both parents declare that they want joint custody. According to the official guidance, these declarations are made, for example, at the Jugendamt or before a notary, and they can be made before the child is born.

Route 2: marriage. If the parents marry each other after the birth, joint custody follows (BGB §1626a(1) no. 2).

Route 3: the family court. On the application of one parent, the court transfers custody, or part of it, to both parents jointly if this does not conflict with the child's welfare ("wenn die Übertragung dem Kindeswohl nicht widerspricht", BGB §1626a(2)). If the other parent puts forward no reasons against joint custody, and none are otherwise apparent, it is presumed that joint custody does not conflict with the child's welfare. The official guidance adds that this applies where no such reasons are raised within a period set by the family court. In that case the court decides in a simplified procedure, without hearing the Jugendamt and without hearing the parents in person.

Recording. For children of unmarried parents, the competent Jugendamt keeps a custody register (Sorgeregister). An entry is made in three cases (SGB VIII §58(1)):
1. when Sorgeerklärungen are made,
2. when a final court decision transfers custody to the parents jointly, in whole or in part, or
3. when a final court decision withdraws custody from the mother, in whole or in part, or transfers it to the father alone.

Advice. Mothers and fathers who are not married to each other are entitled to counselling on making a Sorgeerklärung and on the possibility of a court transfer of joint custody (SGB VIII §18(2)). The official guidance states that your competent Jugendamt advises on all questions of parental custody. That office is the place to start.

rows.question: Where do we apply for Elterngeld in Berlin?
rows.reply:
Under federal law, each state decides which authorities administer Elterngeld (parental allowance). The responsible one is the authority of the district ("des Bezirks") where your child has their residence in Germany when you first apply (BEEG §12(1)). In Berlin, that means the Elterngeldstelle (the state office that decides parental allowance) for your district. The excerpts do not name the individual Berlin offices or their addresses. The Elterngeldstelle decides your application, so it is also where you get a binding answer on your own case.

The law says Elterngeld must be applied for in writing ("Elterngeld ist schriftlich zu beantragen", BEEG §7(1)). The person applying signs the application. The other entitled parent also signs it to confirm they know about it. This does not apply where only one person has custody, or in the case of §4c (BEEG §7(3)).

The consequence of applying late: payment is made retroactively only for "die letzten drei Lebensmonate vor Beginn des Lebensmonats" in which the application was received (BEEG §7(1)). Earlier months are not paid.

There are two ways to apply in Berlin:

1. **Online.** Berlin's service page offers online application. You log in with a BundID account, or register for one if you do not have one. You can sign in with the online ID function (eID) of your ID card, your Unionsbürgerkarte or your electronic residence permit (eAT). The alternatives are an Elster certificate or a username and password. The same page lists, among its conditions, that you live in Berlin and are registered there ("Sie wohnen in Berlin und sind hier gemeldet").

2. **ElterngeldDigital.** This federal service is available in Berlin. A digital assistant helps you fill in the application. You then print it, sign it and post it to your responsible Elterngeldstelle. For technical problems or questions about the application, the ElternDigital support hotline is 0421 - 361 94195, Monday to Thursday, 10-12 and 13-15.

If something changes after you have applied, such as the period of payment or your bank details, Berlin's service page says to use the Berlin change application ("Berliner Änderungsantrag auf Elterngeld").

rows.question: Will our baby automatically be German if we are both Indian citizens?
rows.reply:
Not automatically because of where the baby is born. German Staatsangehörigkeit (citizenship) by birth to parents who are not German depends on conditions that one parent must meet.

The statute gives two routes by birth:

- Through a German parent. Under StAG §4(1), a child acquires German Staatsangehörigkeit by birth if a parent holds German Staatsangehörigkeit.
- Through birth in Germany to foreign parents. Under StAG §4(3), a child of foreign parents born in Germany ("im Inland") acquires German Staatsangehörigkeit if one parent meets both of these conditions: 1. has had lawful habitual residence in Germany for five years ("seit fünf Jahren rechtmäßig seinen gewöhnlichen Aufenthalt im Inland"), and 2. holds an "unbefristetes Aufenthaltsrecht", or, as a Swiss national or a family member of one, holds a residence permit under the EU–Switzerland free movement agreement of 21 June 1999. Both conditions must be met by the same parent. Acquisition is entered in the Geburtenregister in which the child's birth is recorded.

How it is checked (PStV §34):

- When the birth is registered, the Standesamt asks whether a parent holds an "unbefristetes Aufenthaltsrecht" or the Swiss agreement permit.
- If the information given meets that condition, the Standesamt obtains written information from the Ausländerbehörde on whether the information is correct and whether the parent had five years of lawful habitual residence in Germany at the time of the birth.
- The Standesamt also obtains this information if the parents give no details about their status or permit, or if it doubts the details. In that case it asks about both parents.
- The Standesamt then checks whether the child acquired German Staatsangehörigkeit by birth and records the result.

If a child born in Germany does not hold German Staatsangehörigkeit, AufenthG §33 sets out the residence rules:

- The child can be granted a residence permit ex officio if one parent holds an Aufenthaltserlaubnis, a Niederlassungserlaubnis or an Erlaubnis zum Daueraufenthalt – EU.
- The permit is granted ex officio if, at the time of birth, both parents, or the parent with sole custody, hold one of these.
- If the mother or father holds a visa, or may stay without a visa, at the time of birth, the child's stay counts as permitted until that visa or visa-free stay ends.

Whether your baby acquires German Staatsangehörigkeit is not something this service can tell you. It is checked by the Standesamt where the birth is registered, with information from the Ausländerbehörde. The Standesamt is where you get a binding answer on your own child's case.

rows.question: Does our newborn need a residence permit?
rows.reply:
Whether a newborn needs an Aufenthaltserlaubnis (residence permit) depends on the parents' status. The law sets out these rules. Which one applies to your child is not something this answer can decide.

Residence rules for a child born in Germany (AufenthG §33):
1. If one parent holds an Aufenthaltserlaubnis, a Niederlassungserlaubnis or an Erlaubnis zum Daueraufenthalt – EU, the child "kann" (may) be granted an Aufenthaltserlaubnis "von Amts wegen", departing from §§ 5 and 29 Abs. 1 Nr. 2.
2. If, at the time of birth, both parents, or the parent with sole custody ("allein personensorgeberechtigte Elternteil"), hold one of those permits, the child "wird" (is) granted the Aufenthaltserlaubnis "von Amts wegen".
3. If the mother or father holds a visa at the time of birth, or may stay without a visa, the child's stay "gilt ... als erlaubt" (counts as permitted) until that visa or lawful visa-free stay ends.

German citizenship by birth is a separate rule (StAG §4):
- A child acquires German citizenship at birth if one parent is a German citizen (§4(1)).
- A child of foreign parents born in Germany acquires German citizenship if one parent both (1) has had lawful habitual residence in Germany for five years and (2) holds an unbefristetes Aufenthaltsrecht, or, as a Swiss citizen or a Swiss citizen's family member, holds an Aufenthaltserlaubnis under the 1999 EU–Switzerland free-movement agreement (§4(3)). The acquisition is entered in the Geburtenregister where the birth is recorded.

When the birth is registered, the Standesamt asks whether a parent holds such a status (PStV §34(1)). Where the conditions appear to be met, or the parents give no information, or the Standesamt doubts it, it obtains written information from the Ausländerbehörde (PStV §34(2)). The Standesamt then checks whether the child acquired German citizenship and records the result (PStV §34(3)).

The excerpts do not say what applies to a child who falls under none of these rules.

Only the authorities decide your child's case. On citizenship, the Standesamt registering the birth makes the check, so it is where you get a binding answer on that point. For a residence permit, contact your local Ausländerbehörde.

What the statute says. BEEG §3(1) No. 1 lists the Mutterschaftsleistungen that are offset ("angerechnet") against Elterngeld:
- a) Mutterschaftsgeld under the Fifth Book of the Social Code or the Second Act on Farmers' Health Insurance;
- b) the employer's top-up to Mutterschaftsgeld under MuSchG §20.
In both cases this applies to payments due "für die Zeit ab dem Tag der Geburt des Kindes", meaning for the time from the day of the child's birth.

One payment is excluded: the Mutterschaftsgeld under MuSchG §19(2). That is paid by the Bundesamt für Soziale Sicherung, on application, to women who are not members of a statutory health insurer. It is capped at "insgesamt höchstens 210 Euro".

Part months. If the payments are due for only part of a "Lebensmonat des Kindes", they are offset only against the corresponding part of the Elterngeld (BEEG §3(1)).

The 300 euro allowance. BEEG §3(2) leaves Elterngeld free from the offset up to 300 euros. It also says this does not apply where income under §3(1) Nos. 1 to 3 is being offset, and Mutterschaftsgeld falls under No. 1.

What the Familienportal guidance adds:
- Mutterschaftsleistungen for the same child are offset in full. If they are higher than the Elterngeld, only the Mutterschaftsleistungen are paid. If the Elterngeld is higher, the difference is paid as Elterngeld.
- Months in which Mutterschaftsleistungen for the same child are due count as Basiselterngeld months. One day of entitlement in that month is enough.
- Mutterschaftsleistungen are calculated in days and offset to the exact day. If they end partway through a Lebensmonat, Elterngeld is paid proportionally for the remaining days.
- Mutterschaftsleistungen for a different child are offset against only part of the Elterngeld. According to the guidance, 300 euros in Basiselterngeld months and 150 euros in ElterngeldPlus months are not offset.
- A father's Elterngeld drawn during the mother's maternity protection is not reduced. The Mutterschaftsleistungen are offset only against the mother's Elterngeld.

This explains the rule. It does not calculate what you would receive.

rows.question: Can I work while receiving Elterngeld?
rows.reply:
Yes, within limits set by the law.

Who can receive it. One condition for Elterngeld (parental allowance) is that the person "keine oder keine volle Erwerbstätigkeit ausübt": they do no paid work, or do not work full-time (BEEG §1(1) no. 4).

What counts as not working full-time. Under BEEG §1(6), a person is not fully employed if:
1. their working time does not exceed 32 hours a week, averaged over the Lebensmonat ("32 Wochenstunden im Durchschnitt des Lebensmonats");
2. they are in employment for vocational training ("Beschäftigung zur Berufsbildung"); or
3. they work as a suitable childminder within the meaning of §§ 23 and 43 of Book VIII of the Social Code ("geeignete Kindertagespflegeperson").

Under BEEG §1(6a), people who are temporarily not working still count as employed while they are in an employment relationship or are self-employed.

How work affects the payment. BEEG §2(1) states the maximum of 1 800 Euro a month for full Lebensmonate in which the person has no income from work. For Lebensmonate after the birth in which the person earns less than before the birth, Elterngeld is paid as the applicable percentage of the difference between the two incomes. For this purpose, pre-birth income is counted at no more than 2 770 Euro (BEEG §2(3)). The law also allows two Lebensmonate of Elterngeld Plus instead of one Lebensmonat of Basiselterngeld (BEEG §4(3)). The federal family portal says Elterngeld Plus can be especially worthwhile if you work part-time.

What the law requires when you work:
- If your application gives expected income from work, you must prove your actual income for that time after the payment period ends (BEEG §8(1)).
- If you expect income from work during the payment period, the amount is decided provisionally until the required information is proven (BEEG §8(3) no. 3).
- If your application says you will have no income from work, Elterngeld is paid subject to revocation in case you do have such income (BEEG §8(2)).

The family portal says that employees need an employer's certificate of their working hours during the payment period. Self-employed people need their own declaration of their previous working hours and their hours during the payment period.

The portal also says its explanations apply to children born after August 2021. For children born before 1 September 2021, partly different rules apply, and it refers parents to their Elterngeldstelle.

Whether you meet these conditions, and how much you would receive, is decided by your Elterngeldstelle. It is where you get a binding answer on your own case.

rows.question: Where and how do we apply for Kindergeld?
rows.reply:
Where to apply: BKGG §9(1) says the application should be made to the Familienkasse that is competent under §13. Under BKGG §13(1), that is the Familienkasse for the district where the entitled person has their residence ("Wohnsitz"). The fallbacks are:

1. If there is no residence in Germany, the Familienkasse for the district of habitual stay ("gewöhnlicher Aufenthalt").
2. If there is neither, the Familienkasse for the district where the person works.
3. In all other cases, the Familienkasse Bayern Nord.

The same Familienkasse receives the application and decides on the claim (§13(1)). It is where you get a binding answer on your own case. The Familienportal describes it as the Familienkasse of your Agentur für Arbeit.

How to apply: Kindergeld (child benefit) must be applied for in writing ("sind schriftlich zu beantragen", BKGG §9(1)). The Familienportal says the application can be electronic or written, using the Familienkassen's form. You can fill that form in online, then print and sign it. For a newborn, you can also apply fully online with a valid ELSTER certificate, with no printing or handwritten signature.

Who may apply: besides the entitled person, anyone with a legitimate interest in the payment may apply (§9(1)). Kindergeld is paid to only one person per child (BKGG §3(1)). Where a child lives in the parents' joint household, the parents decide between themselves who receives it. If they do not decide, the family court decides on application (§3(2)).

What to provide: the application must give your tax identification number and your child's. For a child under 18, the Bundesagentur für Arbeit says this is normally all you need to provide. For a child born or living abroad, provide a copy of the foreign birth certificate, or another official document certifying the birth. Evidence can be submitted online to your Familienkasse. If it needs more documents, it tells you the date by which to provide them. Missing that date can delay the application or lead to its rejection.

Applying late: the Familienportal says Kindergeld can be paid retroactively for up to 6 months. If you are applying retroactively, state that in the application, along with the date from which you want Kindergeld.

Questions about applying: the Bundesagentur für Arbeit's free service number is 0800 4 555530.

rows.question: What are the Elterngeld rules for a self-employed parent in Bavaria?
rows.reply:
Bavaria is outside the states this product covers. It covers federal law, Hessen's state procedures and the Indian consular track. It cannot tell you how Elterngeld (parental allowance) is applied for or handled in Bavaria. For that, contact the office that handles Elterngeld applications in Bavaria. That office decides individual cases, and it is where you get a binding answer on your own case.

Elterngeld itself is federal law (the BEEG), so the rules below apply in Bavaria as everywhere in Germany.

Who can claim (BEEG §1(1)). A person can claim if they:
1. live or usually stay in Germany,
2. live in one household with the child,
3. care for and bring up the child themselves, and
4. do no work or do not work full-time.

What counts as not working full-time (BEEG §1(6)). A person is not fully employed if:
1. their working time is no more than 32 hours a week, averaged over the child's month of life,
2. they are in employment for vocational training, or
3. they work as a suitable childminder under §§ 23 and 43 SGB VIII.

Self-employed people who are temporarily not working still count as employed (§1(6a) No. 2).

Income limit (BEEG §1(8)). There is no claim if the person's taxable income in the last completed assessment period before the birth was more than 175,000 euros. If another person also meets the household condition, the limit applies to both incomes together.

Which income counts (BEEG §2(1)). The income Elterngeld is based on includes positive income from "Land- und Forstwirtschaft, Gewerbebetrieb und selbständiger Arbeit" (agriculture and forestry, trade or business, and self-employed work). The income must be taxable in Germany. It is reduced by deductions for taxes and social contributions. It is taken as the monthly average over the assessment period under §2b, which is not among these excerpts. The detailed rules are in §§2c to 2f. §2c covers employees' income only.

Amounts (BEEG §2):
- Elterngeld is 67 percent of income before the birth.
- It is paid up to a maximum of 1,800 euros a month for full months with no income from work.
- Below 1,000 euros of pre-birth income, the percentage rises, up to 100 percent.
- Above 1,200 euros, it falls, down to 65 percent.
- If you earn less after the birth than before, Elterngeld is paid on the difference. For this, pre-birth income counts up to 2,770 euros at most.
- The minimum is 300 euros.

Provisional decisions (BEEG §8(3)). The amount is decided provisionally, based on the information you have made credible, until proof is provided, where:
1. the tax assessment notice for the last completed assessment period before the birth is not available at application, and it cannot yet be said whether the §1(8) limits are exceeded,
2. income from work before the birth cannot be determined, or
3. you expect to have income from work during the payment period.

Proof and revocation (BEEG §8(1) and (2)). If the application gave expected income from work, you must prove your actual income for that period after the payment period ends. Elterngeld is paid subject to revocation in two cases:
- you stated you would have no income from work but then do, or
- the tax assessment notice is not available and the application indicates the §1(8) limits will not be exceeded, but they are.

This does not say what you would receive or whether you qualify. The office that handles Elterngeld in Bavaria decides that.

- It must be made in writing: "Elterngeld ist schriftlich zu beantragen" (BEEG §7(1)).

The responsible authority is the one your state designates to carry out the Elterngeld law, for the district where your child has their residence in Germany when you first apply (BEEG §12(1)). rows.question: Based on our situation, will our Elterngeld application be approved?
rows.reply:
Whether your Elterngeld (parental allowance) application will be approved is a decision on your individual case. This service cannot assess it or predict the outcome. Only the responsible authority decides. That is the Elterngeldstelle for your district, and it is where you get a binding answer on your own case.

What the law says, for everyone:

BEEG §1(1) gives a right to Elterngeld to a person who meets all four of these conditions:
1. they have a residence or habitual abode in Germany ("einen Wohnsitz oder seinen gewöhnlichen Aufenthalt in Deutschland"),
2. they live in one household with the child,
3. they care for and bring up the child themselves, and
4. they do no paid work, or not full-time work ("keine oder keine volle Erwerbstätigkeit").

BEEG §1(6) says a person is not in full-time work if their working time does not exceed 32 hours a week on average over the Lebensmonat. It also covers vocational training and work as a qualified Kindertagespflegeperson.

BEEG §1(7) says a non-EU national without freedom of movement is entitled only if they hold one of the residence titles that subsection lists.

BEEG §1(8) says the right lapses if taxable income in the last completed assessment period before the birth was more than 175 000 euro. Where another person also qualifies, the test is whether both persons' combined taxable income is more than 175 000 euro.

Under BEEG §7(1), Elterngeld must be applied for in writing ("schriftlich zu beantragen"). It is paid retroactively only for the last three Lebensmonate before the Lebensmonat in which the application is received. Applying late loses earlier months of payment.

If you disagree with the decision, you can only have it reviewed by lodging a Widerspruch (objection). You must lodge it in writing with your Elterngeldstelle within one month of receiving the decision.

rows.question: How much tax will we save if I switch to Steuerklasse 3 before the birth?
rows.reply:
This cannot tell you how much tax you would save by switching to tax class III. That is a calculation for your own household, and tax-class choice and its tax effects belong to the Finanzamt or a Steuerberater (tax adviser). This product does not calculate tax or recommend a tax class.

The excerpts do cover how a tax-class change before the birth is treated when parental allowance is calculated:

- Parental allowance is based on an "Elterngeld-Netto", which the Elterngeldstelle calculates itself from your gross income using a simplified method. The result can differ from the net pay on your payslip.
- The income-tax deduction in that calculation takes account of the tax class and any factor under § 39f of the Income Tax Act. Tax class VI is disregarded (BEEG §2e(3)).
- For employment income, the assessment period is "die zwölf Kalendermonate vor dem Kalendermonat der Geburt des Kindes": the twelve calendar months before the month of the birth (BEEG §2b(1)).
- If you changed tax class before the birth, the newest tax class is used. The older one is used only if it applied for longer within the whole assessment period than the newer one. The same applies to other deduction data, such as the number of child allowances.
- A further change of tax class after the birth no longer affects the parental allowance.

Whether and how this changes your own payment is not something stated here. The Elterngeldstelle decides the amount, and the Elterngeldstelle for your district is where you get a binding answer on your own case. For the tax side, ask the Finanzamt or a Steuerberater.
